paper.title: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight

claims.paper_claim: FormalJudge improves oversight accuracy by an average of 16.6% over LLM-as-a-Judge baselines across three benchmarks and seven agent models.
claims.paper_production: Run Agent-SafetyBench, VitaBench, and Deceivers with FormalJudge and baseline judges, establish labels, and aggregate accuracy.
claims.limitation: No models, benchmark data, labels, calls, or accuracy aggregation are present.

claims.paper_claim: The main benchmark table reports FormalJudge values including 77.28% and 80.54% on Agent-SafetyBench.
claims.paper_production: Extract atomic facts, synthesize Dafny specifications, execute Dafny/Boogie/Z3, and compare verdicts to benchmark labels.
claims.limitation: No extraction, formal runtime, labels, or independent table is present.

claims.paper_claim: A 7B judge detects deception from 72B agents at above 90% accuracy.
claims.paper_production: Run the Qwen judge-agent matrix on Deceivers, extract atomic deception facts, formally compose predicates, and score 200 deceptive plus 200 non-deceptive trajectories per agent size.
claims.limitation: No Deceivers data, model calls, or weak-to-strong results are present.

claims.paper_claim: Dafny-guided iterative refinement improves accuracy from 70.7% to 99.8% over three rounds.
claims.paper_production: Feed formal specifications and concrete violations back to agents, regenerate for three rounds, and measure safety accuracy.
claims.limitation: No model output, refinement trace, Dafny run, or round metric is present.

claims.paper_claim: Reliability comes from atomic extraction followed by deterministic logical composition.
claims.paper_production: Decompose intent, extract binary grounded facts, generate formal predicates, and let the SMT verifier compute the final verdict.
claims.limitation: The toy uses fixed propositional inputs and Python logic; it has no semantic extraction, Dafny, or Z3.
